sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: On May 3rd, 1978, construction workers in San Francisco were digging a foundation for a new
sentences.zh: 1978年5月3日，旧金山的建筑工人们正在为一栋新建筑挖掘地基，

sentences.en: building on Sansom Street, right next to the tallest skyscraper in the city,
sentences.zh: 地点位于桑森街，紧邻城中最高的摩天大楼，

sentences.en: the Transamerica Pyramid, in the heart of the Financial District.
sentences.zh: 即金融区中心地带的泛美金字塔大厦。

sentences.en: They were about 20 feet below street level when their shovels hit something totally unexpected.
sentences.zh: 当他们挖到地表以下约20英尺深处时，铲子碰到了一个完全意想不到的东西。

sentences.en: It was the hull of an old ship.
sentences.zh: 那是一艘旧船的船体。

sentences.en: That's reporter Emmett Fitzgerald.
sentences.zh: 说话的是记者埃米特·菲茨杰拉德。

sentences.en: Archaeologists immediately came in and started scraping away all the dirt and mud.
sentences.zh: 考古学家们立即赶到现场，开始清理所有的泥土和淤泥。

sentences.en: And, after a few days, they'd uncovered the full skeleton of a 120-foot Gold Rush-era vessel called the Niantic,
sentences.zh: 几天后，他们发掘出了一艘长120英尺的淘金热时期船只的完整残骸，名为“尼亚提克号”，

sentences.en: preserved perfectly in the earth beneath the streets of San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 它在旧金山街道下方的泥土中被完美地保存了下来。

sentences.en: As the archaeologists did their work, hundreds of people gathered to watch the bizarre scene,
sentences.zh: 随着考古学家们的工作展开，数百人聚集在一起观看这奇特的场景，

sentences.en: a massive, massive ship being pulled out from beneath the pavement.
sentences.zh: 一艘巨大无比的船正从路面下被拉出来。

sentences.en: As the construction hoarding was put up, people were carving holes in it to look in and see
sentences.zh: 当建筑围挡竖起后，人们在上面凿出小孔，想要窥探并目睹

sentences.en: Niantic emerge from the mud.
sentences.zh: “尼亚提克号”从泥土中重见天日。

sentences.en: That's James Delgado.
sentences.zh: 说话的是詹姆斯·德尔加多。

sentences.en: I'm an archaeologist and a historian, and I'm the author of Gold Rush Port,
sentences.zh: 我是一名考古学家兼历史学家，也是《淘金热港口：

sentences.en: the Maritime Archaeology of San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 旧金山海洋考古学》一书的作者。

sentences.en: Delgado was 20 years old then, an archaeologist in training,
sentences.zh: 当时的德尔加多才20岁，还是一名实习考古学家，

sentences.en: and he was part of the excavation that day.
sentences.zh: 那天他参与了这次发掘工作。

sentences.en: Inside the ship, he found all kinds of artifacts from the Gold Rush that had been preserved underground.
sentences.zh: 在船内，他发现了各种淘金热时期的文物，它们在地底下保存完好。

sentences.en: Bricks, nails, tin plates for sheathing, boots, jackets, saddles, shovels.
sentences.zh: 砖块、钉子、用于船体覆盖的锡板、靴子、夹克、马鞍、铲子。

sentences.en: A lot of booze.
sentences.zh: 还有很多酒。

sentences.en: 49ers like to drink.
sentences.zh: 淘金客们很爱喝酒。

sentences.en: Delgado even popped the cork on a bottle of 150-year-old champagne.
sentences.zh: 德尔加多甚至撬开了一瓶150年前的香槟。

sentences.en: Tasted awful.
sentences.zh: 味道糟透了。

sentences.en: But the excavation of the Niantic launched his career in marine archaeology
sentences.zh: 但“尼亚提克号”的发掘开启了他的海洋考古生涯，

sentences.en: and inspired him to study the ships beneath San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 并激励他去研究旧金山地下的那些沉船。

sentences.en: Because the Niantic isn't the only one down there.
sentences.zh: 因为地下的船不止“尼亚提克号”这一艘。

sentences.en: I'd say that there are probably as many as 70 ships that were buried
sentences.zh: 我认为可能有多达70艘船被埋在下面，

sentences.en: that in some way, shape, or form remain, even if it's fragments.
sentences.zh: 它们以某种形式留存至今，哪怕只是残骸碎片。

sentences.en: In 1994, city workers were digging a tunnel for the Muni train
sentences.zh: 1994年，市政工人在挖掘穆尼地铁隧道时，

sentences.en: when they hit the side of another Gold Rush ship, the Roam.
sentences.zh: 撞到了另一艘淘金热时期的船——“罗马号”的侧面。

sentences.en: And the decision was made to drill through it.
sentences.zh: 最终决定直接钻穿它。

sentences.en: They tunneled right through the hull.
sentences.zh: 他们直接从船体中间挖了过去。

sentences.en: And today, thousands of San Franciscans travel through the ship every morning
sentences.zh: 如今，成千上万的旧金山人每天早上乘坐火车，

sentences.en: as they ride the train between Folsom Street and the Embarcadero.
sentences.zh: 往返于福尔瑟姆街和内河码头之间，穿过这艘船。

sentences.en: It's not really marked in the tunnel, but for those of us who know,
sentences.zh: 隧道里并没有特别标注，但对于我们这些知情者来说，

sentences.en: when you take that turn, you're passing through the Gold Rush ship, Roam.
sentences.zh: 当你转过那个弯时，你正穿过那艘淘金热时期的船——“罗马号”。

sentences.en: To understand how all of these ships ended up buried underground beneath the city,
sentences.zh: 要了解这些船是如何最终被埋在城市地下的，

sentences.en: we need to go back to the 1830s.
sentences.zh: 我们需要回到19世纪30年代。

sentences.en: When San Francisco was just a tiny little port called Yerba Buena.
sentences.zh: 那时旧金山只是一个名为“耶尔巴布埃纳”的小港口。

sentences.en: It was an outpost of a few buildings with a tiny town square, that's it.
sentences.zh: 它只是一个拥有几栋建筑和一个小镇广场的前哨站，仅此而已。

sentences.en: By 1847, the population had grown to a few hundred.
sentences.zh: 到1847年，人口增长到了几百人。

sentences.en: They renamed the port San Francisco, but it was still just a small town.
sentences.zh: 他们将港口更名为旧金山，但那依然只是个小镇。

sentences.en: But in 1848, all of that changed with the discovery of gold in January.
sentences.zh: 然而1848年1月黄金的发现改变了一切。

sentences.en: The Gold Rush brought a tidal wave of prospectors to California.
sentences.zh: 淘金热为加州带来了一波又一波的探矿者。

sentences.en: And by the end of 1850, the San Francisco waterfront was clogged with more than a thousand ships,
sentences.zh: 到1850年底，旧金山海滨挤满了上千艘船只，

sentences.en: and the town had grown into a city of thousands.
sentences.zh: 而这个小镇也发展成了一座拥有数千人口的城市。

sentences.en: So you're looking at a city that within a decade has gone from being a village
sentences.zh: 所以你看到的是一座在十年内从村庄

sentences.en: to being the 12th largest city in North America.
sentences.zh: 一跃成为北美第12大城市的城市。

sentences.en: But the land around San Francisco was mostly sandy hills,
sentences.zh: 但旧金山周边的土地大多是沙丘，

sentences.en: and not well suited to this scale of development.
sentences.zh: 并不适合这种规模的开发。

sentences.en: So to meet the surging demand for real estate,
sentences.zh: 因此，为了满足激增的房地产需求，

sentences.en: the city sold off plots of water in the shallow tidal zone.
sentences.zh: 市政府出售了潮汐带浅水区的地块。

sentences.en: A person could buy a piece of water, but it was their job to turn it into usable ground.
sentences.zh: 人们可以买下一片水域，但将其变成可用土地是买家的任务。

sentences.en: Some people dumped sand or garbage into their plots to try and make land.
sentences.zh: 有些人往地块里倾倒沙子或垃圾，试图造地。

sentences.en: Others drove stakes into the mud and built platforms on top of the water.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则在泥里打桩，在水面上搭建平台。

sentences.en: And a lot of people repurposed the ships that had brought them to California.
sentences.zh: 还有许多人重新利用了那些载他们来到加州的船只。

sentences.en: The ships helped because as they came, many of them were sitting idle.
sentences.zh: 这些船很有用，因为它们抵达后，许多都处于闲置状态。

sentences.en: The crews had gone off to the diggings or had run away.
sentences.zh: 船员们要么去挖金矿了，要么逃跑了。

sentences.en: So the owners rented them out or sold them outright to become floating houses,
sentences.zh: 于是船主们把它们租出去或直接卖掉，改造成水上住宅、

sentences.en: warehouses, the town jail offices, you name it.
sentences.zh: 仓库、镇监狱、办公室，应有尽有。

sentences.en: Over 200 of them became floating buildings.
sentences.zh: 超过200艘船变成了水上建筑。

sentences.en: Ships were the centers of commercial life in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 船只曾是旧金山商业生活的中心。

sentences.en: Well, you had the Apollo Saloon, which was basically a restaurant.
sentences.zh: 比如“阿波罗沙龙”，它本质上就是一家餐馆。

sentences.en: They sold a donut and a cup of coffee for two bits, they said.
sentences.zh: 据说他们卖一个甜甜圈和一杯咖啡只要两角五分钱。

sentences.en: You had the Euphemia, which was turned into the town jail and later became an insane asylum.
sentences.zh: 还有“尤菲米娅号”，它被改成了镇监狱，后来又变成了精神病院。

sentences.en: You also had ships that served as water cisterns.
sentences.zh: 还有一些船被用作储水罐。

sentences.en: You had other ships that worked as government offices.
sentences.zh: 还有其他船充当政府办公室。

sentences.en: And another ship, the good ship Panama, was used as a seamen's church.
sentences.zh: 另一艘船，著名的“巴拿马号”，被用作海员教堂。

sentences.en: The city looked like a forest of masts.
sentences.zh: 当时的城市看起来就像一片桅杆森林。

sentences.en: And planks connected the ships, creating a grid of boardwalks perched above the water.
sentences.zh: 木板连接着船只，在水面上形成了一个木栈道网。

sentences.en: One visitor said that San Francisco was a Venice built of pine.
sentences.zh: 一位游客曾说，旧金山是一座用松木建造的威尼斯。

sentences.en: But there were obvious downsides to a floating city.
sentences.zh: 但水上城市也有明显的弊端。

sentences.en: And little by little, people began to fill in areas between the ships,
sentences.zh: 于是人们开始一点一点地填平船只之间的区域，

sentences.en: using whatever they could get their hands on.
sentences.zh: 利用一切能弄到的东西。

sentences.en: From garbage to unwanted cargo to dead bodies, you name it, everything was thrown into that.
sentences.zh: 从垃圾到废弃货物，再到尸体，什么都往里扔。

sentences.en: And with this, gradually began the process of filling in the mudflats.
sentences.zh: 随着这些举动，填平泥滩的过程逐渐开始了。

sentences.en: In this way, the shoreline itself began to advance.
sentences.zh: 就这样，海岸线开始向前推进。

sentences.en: At this point, the harbor was a patchwork of freshly filled lots, ships, and buildings on stilts.
sentences.zh: 当时，港口是一片由新填地块、船只和高脚屋组成的拼凑体。

sentences.en: But then, in May of 1851, a massive fire broke out in downtown San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 但到了1851年5月，旧金山市中心爆发了一场大火。

sentences.en: The wind fanned the flames.
sentences.zh: 风助火势。

sentences.en: And by the time the next day had dawned, more than 2,000 buildings were gone.
sentences.zh: 等到第二天黎明时，已有超过2000栋建筑化为乌有。

sentences.en: The flames were so high that they could see the glow in Monterey 100 miles south.
sentences.zh: 火焰高到连100英里外的蒙特雷都能看到火光。

sentences.en: Some of the ships caught fire and sank, leaving their half-charred hulls in the muddy water.
sentences.zh: 一些船只起火沉没，留下了半焦的船体在泥水中。

sentences.en: By the time they managed to put the fire out, the waterfront was just a mushy mess of smoldering timber.
sentences.zh: 当人们终于扑灭大火时，海滨只剩下一片阴燃木材的泥泞废墟。

sentences.en: And that mushy mess was too unstable to rebuild on.
sentences.zh: 而那片泥泞废墟太不稳定，无法在上面重建。

sentences.en: So they used some of the world's first steam-powered excavators
sentences.zh: 于是他们使用了世界上最早的一些蒸汽挖掘机，

sentences.en: to scrape sand off of nearby hills and dunes and dump it on top.
sentences.zh: 从附近的丘陵和沙丘上刮下沙子，倾倒在上面。

sentences.en: By September of 1851, the old waterfront had been completely buried.
sentences.zh: 到1851年9月，旧海滨已被完全掩埋。

sentences.en: And with it, the Niantic, the Rome, and all of the other gold rush ships,
sentences.zh: 随之被埋葬的还有“尼亚提克号”、“罗马号”以及所有其他淘金热时期的船只，

sentences.en: entombed in this manufactured ground.
sentences.zh: 它们被封存在这片人造土地之下。

sentences.en: After the fire, San Francisco continued to expand,
sentences.zh: 大火之后，旧金山继续扩张，

sentences.en: filling in more and more of the tidal zone in deeper and deeper water.
sentences.zh: 在更深的水域填平了越来越多的潮汐带。

sentences.en: And eventually, the state stepped in.
sentences.zh: 最终，州政府介入了。

sentences.en: They built a seawall to cap the production of new land.
sentences.zh: 他们修建了一道海堤来限制新土地的产生。

sentences.en: They drew a line and said, San Francisco, you can go no further.
sentences.zh: 他们划定了一条线，告诉旧金山：不能再往外扩了。

sentences.en: And today, we know that line.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们都知道那条线。

sentences.en: It's the Embarcadero.
sentences.zh: 那就是内河码头。

sentences.en: The walkway along the eastern edge of the San Francisco Wharf.
sentences.zh: 沿着旧金山码头东侧的步道。

sentences.en: But by that time, a city had built up on top of all this sand and dirt and garbage.
sentences.zh: 但那时，一座城市已经建立在这些沙子、泥土和垃圾之上了。

sentences.en: And over the years, San Francisco continued to develop.
sentences.zh: 多年来，旧金山持续发展。

sentences.en: And today, what had been the tidal zone is the heart of the city's financial district.
sentences.zh: 如今，曾经的潮汐带已成为该市金融区的核心。

sentences.en: Throughout history, the absence of ground has proven to be a surprisingly small obstacle
sentences.zh: 纵观历史，对于想要建造东西的人来说，

sentences.en: for people who want to build stuff.
sentences.zh: 缺乏土地已被证明是一个微不足道的障碍。

sentences.en: San Francisco isn't the only city that has built its own land.
sentences.zh: 旧金山并不是唯一一座通过造地建成的城市。

sentences.en: Large portions of Boston, Seattle, Hong Kong, and Mercei were built on top of fill.
sentences.zh: 波士顿、西雅图、香港和默西的大部分地区都是建立在填海造陆之上的。

sentences.en: It's not uncommon to see it in other cities.
sentences.zh: 在其他城市看到这种情况并不罕见。

sentences.en: New York, Manhattan built out and filled.
sentences.zh: 纽约曼哈顿也是向外扩张并填海建成的。

sentences.en: The area the World Trade Center sits on was landfill.
sentences.zh: 世界贸易中心所在的区域就是填海造出来的。

sentences.en: They actually found a ship when they were building the original World Trade Center towers.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们在建造最初的世界贸易中心双子塔时，也发现了一艘船。

sentences.en: What is now Mumbai, India, used to be a seven-island archipelago
sentences.zh: 现在的印度孟买，曾经是一个由七个岛屿组成的群岛，

sentences.en: before the British colonial government turned it all into one contiguous strip of land.
sentences.zh: 后来英国殖民政府将其全部连接成了一片连续的陆地。

sentences.en: Tokyo has built 60,000 acres of new land over the last several centuries.
sentences.zh: 过去几个世纪里，东京建造了6万英亩的新土地。

sentences.en: The process of building new land along the waterfront is often referred to as land reclamation.
sentences.zh: 在海滨建造新土地的过程通常被称为“填海造陆”。

sentences.en: Which is kind of ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 这听起来有点荒谬。

sentences.en: Land reclamation is another one of those words that's made up and it masquerades what's really happening.
sentences.zh: “填海造陆”是那种虚构出来的词汇之一，它掩盖了正在发生的真实情况。

sentences.en: You're creating land where it didn't exist before.
sentences.zh: 你是在原本不存在的地方创造土地。

sentences.en: Or even creating a whole country, like the Netherlands.
sentences.zh: 甚至是在创造一个国家，比如荷兰。

sentences.en: There's a very extraordinary history of basically the Dutch making their own country.
sentences.zh: 荷兰人基本上是靠自己创造了一个国家，这有着非常非凡的历史。

sentences.en: That's Stephen Graham, professor of cities and society at Newcastle University
sentences.zh: 说话的是斯蒂芬·格雷厄姆，纽卡斯尔大学城市与社会学教授，

sentences.en: and author of the book Vertical, The City from Satellites to Bunkers.
sentences.zh: 也是《垂直：从卫星到地堡的城市》一书的作者。

sentences.en: I mean, most of Holland, most of the Netherlands as it's currently constructed
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，荷兰的大部分地区，目前所构建的荷兰大部分国土，

sentences.en: is an engineering construction.
sentences.zh: 都是一项工程建设。

sentences.en: It's a huge project of land reclamation and land manufacture.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的填海造陆和土地制造工程。

sentences.en: The Dutch developed incredible techniques to build land in places that were actually below sea level.
sentences.zh: 荷兰人开发了令人难以置信的技术，在实际上低于海平面的地方建造土地。

sentences.en: And this has been going on since medieval times, where large dikes were constructed,
sentences.zh: 这种情况从中世纪就开始了，当时人们建造了大型堤坝，

sentences.en: large pumping systems were constructed, to create a dry country underneath the sea.
sentences.zh: 建立了大型泵送系统，从而在海平面以下创造了一个干燥的国家。

sentences.en: And the Dutch are proud of this history.
sentences.zh: 荷兰人对这段历史感到自豪。

sentences.en: There's a popular saying there, God created the world, but the Dutch created the Netherlands.
sentences.zh: 那里有一句流行的话：上帝创造了世界，但荷兰人创造了荷兰。

sentences.en: Humans have been making their own ground for a long time,
sentences.zh: 人类制造土地已经很久了，

sentences.en: but the process has reached new heights in recent years.
sentences.zh: 但近年来这一过程达到了新的高度。

sentences.en: The historic scale of land reclamation and land manufacture and the building up of land beneath cities
sentences.zh: 历史上填海造陆、土地制造以及城市下方土地堆积的规模，

sentences.en: is absolutely minuscule compared to the scale at which it's going on today.
sentences.zh: 与今天正在进行的规模相比，简直微不足道。

sentences.en: More and more cities are building waterfront property for airports, skyscrapers and housing.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的城市正在为机场、摩天大楼和住房开发海滨地产。

sentences.en: It's sheer urban economics because you create new supply in an area where there's amazing levels of demand
sentences.zh: 这纯粹是城市经济学，因为你在需求惊人的地区创造了新的供应，

sentences.en: and therefore it's very profitable.
sentences.zh: 因此利润非常丰厚。

sentences.en: And new dredging technologies have enabled developers to build land faster and on a grander scale,
sentences.zh: 新的疏浚技术使开发商能够更快、更大规模地造地，

sentences.en: often at the expense of the environment.
sentences.zh: 但这往往是以牺牲环境为代价的。

sentences.en: I mean, they use huge ships, for example, which have what they call rainbow dredging systeMs.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们使用巨大的船只，例如，配备了所谓的“彩虹疏浚系统”。

sentences.en: These ships suck up massive amounts of sand and gravel from the seafloor
sentences.zh: 这些船从海底吸入大量的沙子和砾石，

sentences.en: and shoot it through the air in a giant arcing rainbow of muck onto the area where they're trying to build new land.
sentences.zh: 然后将它们喷射到空中，形成一道巨大的泥浆彩虹，落在他们试图造地的区域。

sentences.en: This technology has been particularly useful for creating artificial islands.
sentences.zh: 这项技术在建造人工岛方面特别有用。

sentences.en: China is using these rainbow dredging ships to turn uninhabited coral atolls in the middle of the South China Sea
sentences.zh: 中国正在利用这些彩虹疏浚船，将南海中部无人居住的珊瑚环礁，

sentences.en: into larger islands that could support human settlement.
sentences.zh: 变成可以支持人类居住的更大岛屿。

sentences.en: They're actually manufacturing land in the hopes of staking territorial claim to highly contested waters.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上是在制造土地，希望能对高度争议的水域宣示领土主权。

sentences.en: And then there's Dubai.
sentences.zh: 还有迪拜。

sentences.en: Dubai is a poster child for this process, really.
sentences.zh: 迪拜确实是这个过程的典型代表。

sentences.en: The wealthy desert emirate has built a series of artificial islands for wealthy elites.
sentences.zh: 这个富有的沙漠酋长国为富有的精英们建造了一系列人工岛。

sentences.en: Three of the new landforms are shaped like massive palm fronds.
sentences.zh: 其中三个新地貌的形状像巨大的棕榈叶。

sentences.en: Another project, called The World, is a cluster of islands designed to look like a map of the world from above.
sentences.zh: 另一个名为“世界岛”的项目，是一组从高空俯瞰时看起来像世界地图的岛屿。

sentences.en: But Dubai's reclamation project has stirred up so much sediment that they've buried coral reefs, oyster beds, and seagrass fields in the Persian Gulf.
sentences.zh: 但迪拜的填海工程搅动了大量沉积物，掩埋了波斯湾的珊瑚礁、牡蛎床和海草场。

sentences.en: And some of the islands that make up the world are already starting to erode back into the sea.
sentences.zh: 而且构成“世界岛”的一些岛屿已经开始侵蚀，重新沉入大海。

sentences.en: Dubai is also running out of sand.
sentences.zh: 迪拜的沙子也快用完了。

sentences.en: At least, the kind of sand you need to build things.
sentences.zh: 至少，是那种建筑所需的沙子。

sentences.en: Desert sand is too fine for construction.
sentences.zh: 沙漠里的沙子太细，不适合建筑使用。

sentences.en: And Dubai has used up so much of the sand around its coast that they now have to import it from Australia.
sentences.zh: 迪拜已经耗尽了海岸附近的大量沙子，现在不得不从澳大利亚进口。

sentences.en: Globally, humans use over 40 billion tons of sand a year.
sentences.zh: 全球范围内，人类每年消耗超过400亿吨沙子。

sentences.en: The two largest uses of that sand are concrete production and land manufacturing projects.
sentences.zh: 其中两大用途是生产混凝土和土地制造项目。

sentences.en: And it's created a global sand shortage that is forcing countries to go to extreme lengths in their efforts to build new ground.
sentences.zh: 这引发了全球性的沙子短缺，迫使各国为了建造新土地而不惜采取极端手段。

sentences.en: The most famous example here is Singapore.
sentences.zh: 最著名的例子就是新加坡。

sentences.en: The wealthy island nation is one of the densest countries in the world.
sentences.zh: 这个富裕的岛国是世界上人口最稠密的国家之一。

sentences.en: And it's constantly looking to expand its territory.
sentences.zh: 它一直在寻求扩张领土。

sentences.en: There's plans to make Singapore at 20 or 30 percent bigger over the next 40 or 50 years through manufacturing new land.
sentences.zh: 计划通过制造新土地，在未来40到50年内将新加坡的面积扩大20%到30%。

sentences.en: Without enough sand of its own, Singapore has had to look elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 由于自身沙子不足，新加坡不得不向别处寻找。

sentences.en: There's been a lot of evidence that the extended land manufacturing around Singapore, the basis for its growth as a tiny island city,
sentences.zh: 有大量证据表明，新加坡周围大规模的土地制造——这是其作为一个微型岛屿城市增长的基础——

sentences.en: is based on basically stealing sandy islands from the poorer countries like Cambodia and Indonesia and Burma.
sentences.zh: 基本上是建立在从柬埔寨、印度尼西亚和缅甸等较贫穷国家窃取沙岛的基础上。

sentences.en: And then moving the material physically.
sentences.zh: 然后将这些物质进行物理搬运。

sentences.en: Land itself is flowing from poorer countries to wealthier ones.
sentences.zh: 土地本身正从较贫穷的国家流向较富裕的国家。

sentences.en: Those countries have made sand exports illegal because of this sense that they are losing their own territory.
sentences.zh: 由于意识到自己的领土正在流失，这些国家已经宣布沙子出口为非法。

sentences.en: Land manufacturing isn't just expanding territory outward.
sentences.zh: 土地制造不仅仅是向外扩张领土。

sentences.en: In some cases, it's expanding upward.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，它是在向上扩张。

sentences.en: On the coast of Nigeria, developers are building a new luxury city called Eco-Atlantic on top of manufactured ground.
sentences.zh: 在尼日利亚海岸，开发商正在人造地面上建造一座名为“生态大西洋”的新豪华城市。

sentences.en: And the startling thing about Eco-Atlantic is that it's about three or four meters higher than the rest of Lagos.
sentences.zh: 关于“生态大西洋”最令人震惊的是，它比拉各斯其他地区高出约三到四米。

sentences.en: And it's being designed to be more resilient to expected sea level rises than the rest of the city.
sentences.zh: 它的设计初衷是比城市其他地区更能抵御预期的海平面上升。

sentences.en: Lagos is a very poor, low-lying city that's extremely vulnerable to sea level rise.
sentences.zh: 拉各斯是一个非常贫穷的低洼城市，极易受到海平面上升的影响。

sentences.en: So there's a very disturbing,
sentences.zh: 所以这里出现了一种非常令人不安的、

sentences.en: sort of almost apartheid geography emerging here where elites are able to build their own escape routes from increasingly perilous conditions through going higher into manufactured land.
sentences.zh: 某种近乎种族隔离的地理现象，精英们通过向更高的人造土地发展，为自己建造了逃离日益危险环境的路线。

sentences.en: In theory, building new land could be a part of the solution to sea level rise.
sentences.zh: 从理论上讲，建造新土地可能是应对海平面上升的解决方案的一部分。

sentences.en: But Stephen Graham says these new land projects are often built exclusively for the rich.
sentences.zh: 但斯蒂芬·格雷厄姆表示，这些新土地项目往往是专门为富人建造的。

sentences.en: They are being built as private projects for those who can get in and can afford it.
sentences.zh: 它们作为私人项目建造，只为那些能进入并负担得起的人服务。

sentences.en: They're not being built as public projects very often to protect cities as a whole.
sentences.zh: 它们很少作为公共项目来保护整个城市。

sentences.en: Massive reclamation projects like Eco-Atlantic are the most obvious examples of manufactured land.
sentences.zh: 像“生态大西洋”这样的大规模填海工程是人造土地最明显的例子。

sentences.en: But even if you live far away from the coast, the ground beneath your feet may have been partially created by humans.
sentences.zh: 但即使你住得离海岸很远，你脚下的土地也可能是人类部分创造的。

sentences.en: People are continuously impacting the surface of the earth.
sentences.zh: 人类一直在影响地球表面。

sentences.en: We dig up rock from one place, grind it into cement, and build a sidewalk somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 我们从一个地方挖出岩石，磨成水泥，然后在另一个地方铺设人行道。

sentences.en: We blow up skyscrapers, dump the rubble somewhere, and build a hospital on top of it.
sentences.zh: 我们炸掉摩天大楼，把瓦砾倒在某处，然后在上面盖起医院。

sentences.en: And all of this human activity has actually created a new layer on the surface of the earth's cruSt.
sentences.zh: 所有这些人类活动实际上已经在地球地壳表面创造了一个新层。

sentences.en: It's made up of old bricks, ground up cement, and rusting metal.
sentences.zh: 它由旧砖块、磨碎的水泥和生锈的金属组成。

sentences.en: Archaeologists and geologists have started calling this layer the Archaeosphere.
sentences.zh: 考古学家和地质学家开始将这一层称为“考古圈”。

sentences.en: The Archaeosphere isn't totally unnatural.
sentences.zh: “考古圈”并非完全不自然。

sentences.en: It's filled with soil and roots and earthworMs.
sentences.zh: 它充满了土壤、树根和蚯蚓。

sentences.en: Sometimes grass grows on top of it.
sentences.zh: 有时上面还会长出草。

sentences.en: And that makes it hard for us to notice.
sentences.zh: 这让我们很难察觉到它。

sentences.en: Stephen Graham says that this idea, that human activity has actually created a geologic layer on the surface of the earth,
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬·格雷厄姆说，人类活动实际上在地球表面创造了一个地质层的观点，

sentences.en: is bringing archaeologists and geologists together.
sentences.zh: 正在将考古学家和地质学家联系在一起。

sentences.en: Traditionally, archaeologists study human artifacts within the ground, while geologists study the ground itself.
sentences.zh: 传统上，考古学家研究地下的文物，而地质学家研究地面本身。

sentences.en: But what if the ground itself was made by humans?
sentences.zh: 但如果地面本身就是由人类制造的呢？

sentences.en: Archaeologists are increasingly working with geologists, and they see the ground as a gradual accumulation of the leftovers.
sentences.zh: 考古学家越来越多地与地质学家合作，他们将地面视为残留物的逐渐堆积。

sentences.en: Obviously, it's the rubbish, it's the bodies of the dead, it's the leftover materials.
sentences.zh: 显然，那是垃圾、死者的遗体，以及剩余的材料。

sentences.en: And it is increasingly part of the built environment.
sentences.zh: 而且它正日益成为建筑环境的一部分。

sentences.en: I think that's really important.
sentences.zh: 我认为这非常重要。

sentences.en: Important for one, because we need to understand what the ground is made of if we want to build safely on top of it.
sentences.zh: 首先很重要，因为如果我们想在上面安全地建造，就需要了解地面是由什么构成的。

sentences.en: Manufactured ground can be unstable and more susceptible to earthquakes and landslides.
sentences.zh: 人造地面可能不稳定，更容易受到地震和山体滑坡的影响。

sentences.en: For example, in China, in Shenzhen, when the construction material that was heaped up on a hillside as part of the great expansion of that city
sentences.zh: 例如，在中国深圳，当作为城市大扩张的一部分堆积在山坡上的建筑材料

sentences.en: basically slumped down as a great big slide, and I think there was about 80 people killed in that as well.
sentences.zh: 基本上坍塌成了一场巨大的滑坡，我想那次事故中大约有80人丧生。

sentences.en: So we need to become much more aware that in creating our own geology, we're also creating our own hazards.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要更加意识到，在创造我们自己的地质时，我们也在制造我们自己的危险。

sentences.en: But the Archaeosphere is also a resource to be explored.
sentences.zh: 但“考古圈”也是一种值得探索的资源。

sentences.en: There's been estimates that there's as much copper in that artificial ground as there is in all of the copper mines in the world.
sentences.zh: 据估计，这种人造地面中的铜含量与世界上所有铜矿中的铜含量相当。

sentences.en: So in Scandinavia, they're actually starting to mine the disused industrial ground of their own industrial cities.
sentences.zh: 因此在斯堪的纳维亚半岛，他们实际上已经开始开采本国工业城市中废弃的工业用地。

sentences.en: When you walk through a city coated in pavement and covered in buildings,
sentences.zh: 当你走过一座铺满路面、覆盖着建筑物的城市时，

sentences.en: it's easy to assume that the ground beneath you is ancient and natural.
sentences.zh: 很容易认为你脚下的土地是古老而自然的。

sentences.en: There's a tendency always just to see the ground as something that's always been there and always will be there.
sentences.zh: 人们总是倾向于认为地面是某种一直存在且将永远存在的东西。

sentences.en: But there's a huge amount of evidence that cities build their own ground.
sentences.zh: 但有大量证据表明，城市建造了自己的地面。

sentences.en: Cities are agents for making their own geology.
sentences.zh: 城市是制造自身地质的代理人。

sentences.en: If you look at a brand new land reclamation project like Eco-Atlantic, it's obvious the ground is manufactured.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看像“生态大西洋”这样的全新填海项目，很明显地面是人造的。

sentences.en: Right now, it looks like a giant sandy construction site.
sentences.zh: 现在，它看起来像一个巨大的沙质建筑工地。

sentences.en: But if all goes according to plan, pretty soon there will be parking lots and skyscrapers and apartment buildings.
sentences.zh: 但如果一切按计划进行，很快就会有停车场、摩天大楼和公寓楼。

sentences.en: And right now, it's hard to imagine that such a blatant example of artificial ground will one day become seen as just an ordinary part of the Nigerian landscape.
sentences.zh: 而现在，很难想象这样一个明显的人造地面例子，有一天会被视为尼日利亚景观中普通的一部分。

sentences.en: But you probably could have said the same thing about San Francisco in 1850.
sentences.zh: 但你可能对1850年的旧金山也会说同样的话。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Emmett Fitzgerald with Katie Mingle and Sharif Youssef.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99% Invisible》由埃米特·菲茨杰拉德制作，凯蒂·明格尔和谢里夫·优素福协助。

sentences.en: Plus Sam Greenspan, Delaney Hall, Kurt Kolstad, Taryn Mazza, Avery Truffleman, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 还有萨姆·格林斯潘、德莱尼·霍尔、库尔特·科尔斯塔德、塔琳·马扎、艾弗里·特鲁夫曼，以及我，罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Special thanks this week to archaeologist Matt Edgeworth, who's writing about the Archaeosphere helped us a lot on this episode.
sentences.zh: 本周特别感谢考古学家马特·埃奇沃思，他关于“考古圈”的著作对本集节目帮助很大。

sentences.en: Also, Stephen Graham's new book, Vertical, is coming out this fall.
sentences.zh: 此外，斯蒂芬·格雷厄姆的新书《垂直》将于今年秋季出版。

sentences.en: You can find a link to it on our website.
sentences.zh: 你可以在我们的网站上找到链接。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 KALW San Francisco and produced on Radio Row in beautiful downtown.
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山91.7 KALW的一个项目，在美丽的市中心Radio Row制作。

sentences.en: Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚州奥克兰。

sentences.en: We have a lively community on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 我们在Facebook上有一个活跃的社区。

sentences.en: I'm on Twitter at Roman Mars, like way, way, way too much.
sentences.zh: 我在Twitter上的账号是Roman Mars，发得实在太多了。

sentences.en: But if you want hundreds and hundreds of stories to make yourself sound really interesting at parties,
sentences.zh: 但如果你想要成百上千个故事，让自己在聚会上听起来非常有趣，

sentences.en: I recommend you go immediately to 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 我建议你立即访问99pi.org。

sentences.zh: Radiotopia。
